script_text:
This is the Food Line briefing for June 12, 2026.

Today's briefing is based on 3 current public signals selected from 31 reviewed records.

Food insecurity in Horry County is about 14 percent and about 20 percent of children are food insecure, while the Lowcountry Food Bank said some Conway distributions usually serving about 100 families had 185 and demand is climbing at pantries and mobile distributions, with summer strain.

The Horry County signal points to pantry demand and supply strain.

In Tennessee, WKRN reported that reported Tennessee SNAP enrollment fell by more than 100,000 people in less than a year, affecting SNAP households.

In Tulsa, OK, Tulsa Flyer reported that Food Bank of Eastern Oklahoma reported diesel costs of about $24,000–$26,000 per month, compared with about $12,000–$14,000 in typical summer months, reducing meal capacity for children, summer meal recipients, and food-bank clients.

Source links, excerpts, and background references are available in the public source table.

This has been the Food Line briefing from The Blue Fern Co.
episode_summary: Today's Food Line briefing tracks food-bank demand in Horry County. Background and source links are available in the public source table.
